evals.name: new-project-devin-hooks-scaffold
evals.prompt: I have a TypeScript monorepo with pnpm, Turborepo, .envrc, and no Devin hook setup yet. Audit the repo first, verify the live Devin hook docs, then scaffold project hooks in .devin/hooks.v1.json with a generated hooks README and bash stubs for every documented Devin lifecycle event.
evals.expected_output: The response verifies the live official Devin hook docs first, audits the repo in detail, creates a deterministic managed hook scaffold, and wires only the chosen events into .devin/hooks.v1.json.

assertions.text: Response verifies the live official Devin hooks docs before scaffolding
Response audits the project before deciding which events to enable
Response creates one managed bash stub per documented Devin lifecycle event
Generated hook stubs are modular, commented, and expose a clear handle_event edit point
Generated hooks are merged into .devin/hooks.v1.json without a top-level hooks wrapper

evals.name: blocking-policy-exit-code-2
evals.prompt: Set up a Devin PreToolUse hook that blocks dangerous shell commands. I want blocking to use the Devin-documented exit code 2 and not just exit 1.
evals.expected_output: The response uses command hooks that return exit code 2 for intentional blocking and explains that other non-zero codes are logged without blocking.

assertions.text: Response uses exit code 2 for intentional blocking
Response does not use exit code 1 as the blocking mechanism

evals.name: existing-hooks-additive-refresh
evals.prompt: This project already has .devin/hooks.v1.json with a few custom hooks. Add a managed scaffold for Devin lifecycle hooks, but keep the custom hooks unless they are inside the managed generated folder.
evals.expected_output: The response chooses additive mode, preserves non-managed hooks, and refreshes the managed layer only.

assertions.text: Response distinguishes managed hooks from non-managed hooks
Response uses additive mode for a partial refresh

evals.name: avoid-claude-config
evals.prompt: Scaffold Devin CLI hooks, but please do not write Claude Code settings or .claude files. I want the recommended .devin/hooks.v1.json path.
evals.expected_output: The response writes generated hooks to .devin/hooks.v1.json and avoids Claude config paths.

assertions.text: Response uses .devin/hooks.v1.json as the generated hook target

evals.name: matcher-regex-mcp-tools
evals.prompt: I need a Devin hook that applies only to GitHub MCP tools. Use the correct matcher for mcp__github__create_issue and related tools.
evals.expected_output: The response explains that hook matchers are regexes over tool_name and uses a pattern such as ^mcp__github__.*.

assertions.text: Response uses regex matcher syntax for MCP tools
Response does not use permission-glob syntax like mcp__github__*

evals.name: shared-script-adapter-layout
evals.prompt: Scaffold Devin hooks that run the same validation logic I may later use from Codex, OpenCode, Husky, and GitHub Actions. Keep the scripts DRY and path-agnostic.
evals.expected_output: The response places reusable behavior in repo-owned scripts and keeps generated Devin hook files as thin adapters that call those scripts with a harness/mode argument.

assertions.text: Response uses references/reusable-scripts.md for placement guidance
Response keeps generated hook stubs thin and puts reusable behavior under repo-owned scripts

evals.name: docs-drift-detected
evals.prompt: Before scaffolding Devin hooks, confirm whether the live official docs added or removed lifecycle events since the baked-in manifest was written. If they did, update the scaffold inputs first.
evals.expected_output: The response treats the live official Devin docs as the source of truth and refreshes the event manifest before scaffolding if the docs changed.

assertions.text: Response re-verifies the official docs on every real scaffold run
Response does not trust the static manifest without live confirmation

evals.name: hooks-explanation-only
evals.prompt: Explain how I should structure Devin CLI hooks in this project, but do not scaffold or edit anything yet.
evals.expected_output: The response explains the recommended structure and event strategy without generating or editing files.

assertions.text: Response can answer in design mode without scaffolding
Response does not force file creation when the user asked for explanation only
